summary: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
trigger: Post-DONE effect measurement for B-cee5: same story (B-4e16), same harness, old vs new scope-plan template as the only variable.
lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.

summary: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
trigger: done_prepare doneClosure BLOCKED with review_assurance_floor_high_risk_3x2_or_fallback_missing, or quorum_submit refuses with missing current pass lane(s).
lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
reusePrompt: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST

summary: ProofStory DONE shrinkage detector is a regex over summary text; shrinkage-flavored wording about neighboring items falsely blocks DONE.
trigger: story_advance DONE fails with unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage: DONE summary appears narrower than the original snapshot.
lesson: evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (core/proofstory.ts ~1582) flags unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage via a regex matching out of scope, follow-up, not covered, deferred, excluded, partial, narrower etc. in the DONE summary. Describing a NEIGHBORING issue as out of this story scope / spun off as a follow-up in summary limitations trips the gate even when the story delivered everything promised. Fix by rephrasing (the sibling item is a different artifact owned by its own task; this story delivered fully) via summary_set, not by recording a false scope_shrinkage_decision_set.

summary: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
trigger: done_prepare doneClosure BLOCKED with stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch plus review_assurance floor local rounds 0/N right after merging main into a story branch.
lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
reusePrompt: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json

summary: Byte-budget assertions over output containing live machine state are nondeterministic; disable environment-dependent sections in fixtures via their documented env switches.
trigger: A previously green byte-budget smoke (brief-output doctor under 20000 bytes) fails minutes later with a bigger byte count and no code change.
lesson: The doctor brief includes the advisory host burn scan which streams the operator live ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions state, so the smoke byte count varied with session activity (B-fa65 F-004: 20239 then 20606 on identical code). Fix pattern: the fixture invocations set LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 (the scan documented disable switch) on every doctor call so the budget asserts the projection deterministically; the budget value itself stays untouched. Generalization: grep the feature for an env disable switch before patching budgets or output.
reusePrompt: doctor brief under budget got NNNNN / brief-output-smoke nondeterministic / burn scan bytes vary

summary: A PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS repin is not single-source-of-truth even though it looks like one file.
trigger: B-3144: cli-engine.ts changed (new CLI wiring), requiring a repin in retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts's PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS map. That repin alone left validate failing with two unrelated-looking errors (red-evidence-target-binding-smoke.js, red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs) because scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs independently lists every one of those same fingerprint values again, as a flat 'this literal must still appear in source' vocabulary check.
lesson: When repinning ANY structural/AST fingerprint (canonicalAstFingerprint or similar whole-file hash), grep the WHOLE repo for the OLD value before considering the repin done -- do not stop at the first file where you found it. At least two independent mechanisms (the guard's own approval map, and verify-process-fact-contract.mjs's vocabulary list) must both track the same value or validate fails with errors that give zero hint they are fingerprint-related.
reusePrompt: Before or after editing PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS in any *-guard-smoke.ts file, run: grep -rn '<old-fingerprint-value>' . to find every reference, not just the smoke file.

summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest bakes in whatever ad-hoc env vars a command was run with, so a genuinely fresh PASS can still fail the next admissibility check.
trigger: B-3144: ran done_required_validate with LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS env-var overrides set (needed for an earlier, much longer 94-command validate step, not actually needed for this specific 2-command check whose default budget was already generous). Those extra env vars got hashed into the evidence's effectiveEnvironmentDigest (core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment). story_advance --phase=DONE then recomputed the digest WITHOUT those vars and refused with effective-environment-digest-mismatch[0]/[1] -- this happened even on a second, genuinely fresh done_required_validate re-run, because I made the same env-var mistake twice before noticing.
lesson: Do not set ad-hoc env-var overrides (LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, or any other ad-hoc export) on a done_required_validate/validate call unless that SPECIFIC command actually needs a longer budget than its own configured default. Extra env vars are not free -- they get baked into the admissibility digest and will mismatch the next consumer's recomputation, which does not see your shell's exported vars. Check the command's own default timeoutMs first (shown in validate's own progress output) before reaching for an env override.
reusePrompt: Seeing 'Cannot enter DONE: ... effective-environment-digest-mismatch' after a fresh-looking PASS? Check whether the producing command had extra LATTICE_*_TIMEOUT_MS or other env vars exported that the checking command does not have.

summary: A test fixture that 'poisons' state via a synthetic/fake identifier can be silently defused by an unrelated later fix that specifically targets fake or mismatched identifiers.
trigger: B-3144: injectPoisonedDuplicates/appendDuplicatesForRunId (in quorum-submit-smoke.ts) simulated the B-bf52 poisoning incident by tagging duplicate host_verdict rows with a synthetic non-current materialDigest string. B-f88e -- an unrelated, independently-landed sibling fix merged in via main the same day -- added a floor-side guard (eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade liveIdentities skip) that specifically declines to downgrade a stale-material duplicate sharing identity with an already-native verdict. That guard silently neutralized the synthetic-drift fixture: the poisoning stopped reproducing and 3 regression checks (including 2 guarding real security findings F-024/F-025) started passing vacuously, with no test failure to signal it.
lesson: After landing ANY defense-in-depth fix (especially one that specifically detects/ignores fake, stale, or mismatched data), re-audit sibling test fixtures elsewhere in the codebase that simulate the SAME attack/incident class via a similarly-shaped fake identifier -- they may now be silently defused and passing vacuously. This is invisible from a green test run; it only surfaces by re-deriving what the fixture is supposed to prove and checking the fixture still forces that exact condition (e.g. temporarily reverting the new fix and confirming the fixture-under-test genuinely fails again).
reusePrompt: Landed a fix that makes the system correctly ignore/discount fake or stale data? Grep for other test fixtures constructing similarly-fake data to simulate the same incident class, and re-verify each still has real discriminating power.

summary: verification_evidence_add's per-intentRef command pin is permanently immutable, and custom intentRefs must still resolve to an authored PLAN-time verificationIntent -- there is no way to add or strengthen mechanical evidence for a checklist item once REVIEW finds a weak check.
trigger: A REVIEW-phase test-coverage reviewer found 3 verificationIntent entries whose pinned command+selector couldn't actually discriminate the scenario it claimed to test (e.g. a git-diff substring check that would also match a REMOVED line, so it can't tell 'preserved' from 'deleted').
lesson: verification_evidence_add refuses a second command for an already-evidenced intentRef with receipt-command-mismatch (the pin is immutable by design, anti-gaming). It also refuses a brand-new custom intentRef with intent_ref_unresolved unless that ref matches an intent already authored in checklist.json's verificationIntent arrays at PLAN time -- there is no command to append a NEW intent slot to an existing checklist item during REVIEW. When a reviewer finds a weak/non-discriminating pinned check post-hoc, the only real remedy is: (1) check whether a SIBLING intent on the same item already does the strong version of the same check (if so, cite it and resolve as sound-but-redundant); (2) if no sibling exists, independently re-verify the underlying claim by hand right now (a throwaway script/fixture) and record that manual re-verification plus the tooling gap explicitly in the finding_resolve reasoning -- do not try to force a mechanical re-pin, it will just error.
reusePrompt: verification_evidence_add receipt-command-mismatch / intent_ref_unresolved / weak evidence found during REVIEW / can't strengthen pinned checklist evidence / immutable intentRef pin

summary: A new lifecycle-gate artifact written OUTSIDE .lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/ needs its own runtime-artifact-registry entry (materialHash:'exclude') -- autoCommitStoryMetadata never reaches it, and auto-committing the write directly is the wrong fix (moves HEAD, breaks other signed evidence freshness).
trigger: B-a7c5 CHK-003's dev_memory_finish_decision writes to .lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/<storyId>.json, deliberately outside the story dir (it's shared dev-memory infrastructure, not per-story metadata). Left uncommitted after a write, this file fell through dirty-worktree classification to unexpected_dirty_files (blocking) and stranded review_run_start -- found live during REVIEW round 3.
lesson: First instinct was to auto-commit the write inside the handler (mirroring finding_resolve's commitHint/autoCommitStoryMetadata pattern) -- this worked for the immediate symptom but introduced a WORSE regression: the new commit moved HEAD, which retroactively invalidated any test-evidence.json/delivery-check.json already signed against the prior HEAD (stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch), confirmed via a targeted repro before landing. The correct fix is almost always to register the path in core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts (RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY) with materialHash:'exclude', which routes dirty-worktree classification to the non-blocking runtime_artifact_changes category via findRuntimeArtifactEntry, AND ensures the path never perturbs currentMaterialHash in the first place -- no commit-timing/HEAD-movement side effects at all. Only add ignorePatterns if the artifact should ALSO be gitignored; a deliberately git-tracked-but-non-authoritative artifact (like this one) should have ignorePatterns:[] so it stays visible/shareable while still being non-blocking.
reusePrompt: review_run_start / dirty-worktree unexpected_dirty_files / new artifact outside story dir / stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch after auto-commit / RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY materialHash exclude

summary: A materialHash-invariance test that only writeFileSync's (never commits) is non-discriminating: currentMaterialHash reads git ls-tree (committed state), so the assertion passes identically whether or not a runtime-artifact-registry exclusion actually exists.
trigger: B-a7c5's own F-005 regression test (added to prove a new registry exclusion works) only wrote the file, never committed it. A REVIEW quality-lane reviewer caught this in round 4 (F-006): deliberately removing the registry entry and re-running the test showed it still passed, because a bare write never touches HEAD/git ls-tree regardless of whether the exclusion exists.
lesson: When writing a regression test for a materialHash-exclusion fix, the test MUST actually commit the artifact (git add + git commit) and check currentMaterialHash across that commit -- not just before/after a bare write. A write-only invariance check only proves 'writing this file doesn't dirty an in-memory hash', which is trivially true for ANY uncommitted file regardless of registry configuration. Verify a new discriminating assertion's power directly: temporarily break the fix it's supposed to protect, confirm the test fails, then restore and confirm it passes again -- do not trust that an assertion is discriminating just because it currently passes.
reusePrompt: materialHash invariance test / runtime-artifact-registry regression test / currentMaterialHash write vs commit / non-discriminating assertion / verify test catches the bug

summary: lattice.config.json's validate.commands does NOT cover every test file in the repo -- the project's root npm test (full-suite-runner.js, driven by package.json's much longer test:serial-reference script list) is a broader, separate canonical test command that can catch regressions lattice validate and multiple REVIEW rounds all miss.
trigger: B-a7c5's CHK-001 change (a new gate check running before proofStoryDevGateFailure) broke packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts's DEV-admission assertions. 5 REVIEW rounds (4 lattice-review-quality passes + full lattice validate 96/96 green each time) never caught it, because that file is not registered in lattice.config.json's validate.commands. A round-5 quality reviewer caught it only by going beyond the two named fixes under review and running the project's root npm test as due diligence.
lesson: lattice validate (and by extension every REVIEW round that relies on it as its evidence) only exercises whatever is explicitly listed in lattice.config.json's validate.commands array. The project's root package.json 'test' script (full-suite-runner.js) runs a much longer, separately-maintained list that is NOT a subset check against validate.commands -- a file can exist in one list, the other, both, or neither. For any change touching a widely-shared code path (state-machine guards, core registries, shared handler utilities), run the project's root npm test at least once before DONE, not just lattice validate. Also: npm test's own HEAD-drift self-protection aborts the whole run if anything commits mid-run (e.g. a concurrent dev_memory_capture/finding_resolve auto-commit) -- run it with zero concurrent git-mutating commands, or its own protective abort looks like a mass test failure when it is not.
reusePrompt: npm test failing but lattice validate passed / REVIEW rounds missed a regression / validate.commands not comprehensive / full-suite-runner.js / full-suite identity drift HEAD changed during execution

summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
trigger: done-premerge-mainsha-recheck-smoke.ts failed with 'abort: external-advance shim fired (marker written) / the merge-tree interception marker was never created' -- I concluded this was an unrelated, pre-existing merge-tree-shim timing bug (confirmed the file wasn't in my diff, spawned a separate task to fix it). A round-6 quality reviewer added debug instrumentation and found the REAL cause: my own CHK-003 change (a new canFinishGuard check) was blocking the fixture's real story_advance DONE call with missing_dev_memory_finish_decision, BEFORE the story_advance call ever reached the merge-tree pre-check logic the fixture's assertion message was actually about. The fixture's assertion just checks 'did the expected marker get written', which is equally false whether the merge-tree logic never ran OR ran and failed differently -- the message doesn't distinguish those cases.
lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.
reusePrompt: test failure message sounds like infrastructure/environment / tempted to call it unrelated pre-existing / spawn_task for a test failure / verify root cause before triaging as out of scope / shim fired marker never created

summary: execFileSync's pipe-based stdio capture truncates large synchronous crash dumps at 8192 bytes on macOS; spawnSync with a real file descriptor does not.
trigger: Writing a RED reproduction script that captures a large child-process crash dump (a big JSON diagnostics payload embedded in an assert.equal custom message) via execFileSync, then grepping the captured text for a signature that appears near the END of the dump -- the grep silently fails to match because the capture was truncated well before reaching it, with no truncation warning.
lesson: execFileSync's internal pipe-based stdout/stderr capture can silently truncate a large synchronous write from a crashing child process at a small fixed size (observed: exactly 8192 bytes) on macOS, well below its documented maxBuffer default (1MB) -- this is NOT a maxBuffer issue, it is a pipe-buffer/flush-timing issue specific to large synchronous writes right before process exit. The fix: use spawnSync with stdio wired to a real file descriptor (fs.openSync a temp file, pass its fd as stdio[2]) instead of 'pipe', then read the file back with fs.readFileSync -- this captures the full output reliably. Always verify a RED script's assertions actually match by writing captured output to a file and grepping it directly during authoring, not just trusting a truthy exit code.
reusePrompt: Writing a script that captures a child process's crash output via execFileSync and a downstream regex/grep against it isn't matching a string you can see is really there in a manual run / RED script assertion mysteriously fails to match text that should be present in a large crash dump / execFileSync output looks truncated

summary: Rerouting a lock/path argument at a call site can be a no-op if the callee already independently re-derives the same shared root internally.
trigger: Diagnosing a worktree-teardown race by tracing WHERE a lock or path is passed in from, then patching that call site to pass a 'more correct' root, without first checking whether the callee already resolves to the same canonical location on its own.
lesson: acquireStoryTransitionLock(root, storyId) looked like it needed a stable-root reroute to survive a winning DONE deleting the worktree it was called from -- but storyTransitionLockPath already resolves root through resolveSharedLockRoot (git-common-dir based, B-d877 R2 FIX B) BEFORE touching disk, so ANY root string passed in (worktree path or main repo root) resolves to the identical shared lock directory. The reroute compiled, built, and even made the target smoke test pass -- because the REAL fix (a separate StoryArtifactMissingError translation) was landed in the same commit, masking that the reroute itself did nothing. A REVIEW reviewer caught it by comparing storyTransitionLockPath(worktreePath, id) vs storyTransitionLockPath(mainRepoRoot, id) directly and finding them identical. Before adding a 'fix' that reroutes an argument into a shared/lock/root-resolution function, read the CALLEE's own resolution logic first -- if it already normalizes via git-common-dir or similar, the caller-side reroute is redundant. When a test passes after a multi-part fix, that does not mean every part of the fix is load-bearing; isolate and re-test each part before crediting it as the actual fix.
reusePrompt: adding a stable-root/shared-root reroute before a lock or path helper / lock directory disappears with worktree teardown / fix passes tests but reviewer says a change is a no-op / multi-part fix, unclear which part is load-bearing

summary: verification_evidence_add pins a checklist intents evidence command+selector IMMUTABLY on the first selector-bearing write, forever - never bind a selector that embeds a value expected to change (like an assertion count).
trigger: Wrote a selector like "smoke passed: 27 assertions" for 32 verificationIntent items before all coverage was implemented. Later REVIEW findings required adding real assertions (27->33->40->45), and the selector permanently stopped matching - no verification_evidence_add/_batch_add call can ever change a pinned commands command or selector again, even nonMechanicalReason still requires the immutable command to match.
lesson: The only recovery once a bad selector is pinned: go back to PLAN phase and wholesale-replace the affected items verificationIntent via checklist_update (item.verificationIntent = args.verificationIntent is a full overwrite, which clears the embedded .verification pin field on each intent object - confirmed empirically). Then re-pin fresh with a selector that is a STABLE SUBSTRING PREFIX only (e.g. "smoke passed:" not "smoke passed: 27 assertions") so it survives future legitimate growth. kind:waiver bypasses the pin check entirely and satisfies REVIEW-phase gates but NOT the DEV->TEST verification-coverage gate or the DONE ProofStory-acceptance-binding completeness gate, both of which require genuinely mechanical (non-waiver) evidence.
reusePrompt: Seeing receipt-command-mismatch or receipt-selector-mismatch ("the verification pin is immutable") on verification_evidence_add/_batch_add? Or a checklist item stuck needing real coverage after its evidence was already pinned to a stale selector? Search for this lesson.

summary: done_prepare has a convergence invariant that fails if the SAME validation group (commandSetHash+materialHash+storyFilesHash) was executed more than once after TEST entry - repeated retries of a flaky done_required_validate/lattice validate under load pollute unchangedSuiteExecutions.
trigger: done_required_validate kept failing on an unrelated, load-sensitive pre-existing test (different test each time - flow-stability-smoke, review-pass-discard-smoke, validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke - all confirmed passing in isolation, load average was 8-40 on a shared dev machine with multiple concurrent worktree sessions). Retried the SAME command 3+ times at the same material hash until it finally passed. done_prepare --dryRun then failed with done_prepare convergence invariant failed: {unchangedSuiteExecutions:1,...} even though DONE-required validation itself showed PASS.
lesson: unchangedSuiteExecutions counts EXTRA executed terminals for the same validation group within the post-testEntry window (Math.max(0, postTestExecuted.length-1)), so any retry of a flaky validate/done_required_validate at unchanged material after TEST entry poisons it. The only recovery is bouncing the story TEST->DEV->REVIEW->TEST (with no code change) which resets facts.testEntryAt to NOW, excluding all prior executions from the window. REVIEW->DEV requires dev_memory_preflight_ack first (missing_dev_memory_preflight_ack). After the bounce, run done_required_validate/lattice validate EXACTLY ONCE at the new anchor and do not retry even if it fails - if it does fail, bounce again rather than retrying, since a retry-then-pass at the SAME anchor still leaves 2 executions in the window. Prefer waiting for system load to drop (check uptime) before that one critical attempt.
reusePrompt: Seeing "done_prepare convergence invariant failed" with a nonzero unchangedSuiteExecutions (or postTestReviewerReattestations/metadataRollbacks/humanConfirmations) after done_required_validate/lattice validate finally passed post-retries? Search for this lesson before assuming DONE is close.

summary: Hot-main DONE: after merging an actively-moving main, re-run a fresh validate to rewrite canonical evidence to the post-merge head so the net-diff lineage is clean, then autopilot/floor/delivery re-bind at the new materialHash.
trigger: done_prepare BLOCKED at doneClosure/evidenceFreshness with untrusted-lineage-path (main's files) or delivery/floor materialHash-mismatch after a main merge on a busy shared workspace
lesson: 1) A main merge that changes CODE/CHANGELOG changes the story materialHash -> delivery-check + assurance floor stale; other stories' .lattice metadata merges do NOT change materialHash but DO pollute validation lineage. Fix: fresh validate re-baselines canonical evidence to the current head (clean net-diff), then autopilot_review_submit x3 + review_escalation_fallback_set re-bind the floor, and re-sign delivery. 2) verification evidence binds to storyFilesHash so every metadata commit stales it -> refresh it LAST, chained directly into done_prepare. 3) content-binding's real-rebuild refresh (~84 rebuilds) exceeds the 15min plain-validate/refresh MAX -> raise LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS on validate/refresh (never on done_prepare). 4) convergence invariant trips on duplicate post-TEST-entry suite executions from the cascade -> re-anchor TEST->DEV->REVIEW->TEST resets testEntryAt. 5) v0.3.258 added new DEV gate (dev_memory_preflight_ack) and DONE gate (dev_memory_finish_decision).
reusePrompt: hot main merge DONE cascade lineage freshness re-anchor B-1734

summary: A smoke can print PASS then still fail the suite because success-path rmSync throws macOS ENOTEMPTY.
trigger: validate.commands[N] fails with ENOTEMPTY after the smoke already printed passed; isolated reruns of the same file exit 0.
lesson: If a smoke builds a git-backed tmpdir of hundreds or thousands of files, put maxRetries/retryDelay on every rmSync, including the success-path cleanup OUTSIDE the try/catch. A throw there is an unhandled exception and a non-zero exit even though every assertion passed. Isolated reruns often miss it; it shows up under serial validate load. Same pattern as validation-reuse-merge-lineage-smoke rmScratch.
reusePrompt: material-hash-large-tree ENOTEMPTY after smoke passed / success-path rmSync outside try / validate command failed isolated rerun passed

summary: A guarantee restated in prose next to the code it describes goes stale, and each fix's own new prose carries the next instance.
trigger: You are about to write or repair a comment, docstring or decision document that states a property of nearby code - a bound, a count, a cap, an invariant, or what a function cannot do.
lesson: B-3434 spent twelve review rounds and forty-one findings on ONE defect wearing eight costumes: wrong values, a duplicated details copy the bound ignored, key names the bound did not cover, a GUARANTEED paragraph the code did not provide, the serialization boundary, the try/catch scope, an inherited prototype, and a work order that prescribed the very duplication it declared closed. Round 9 - the round reviewing round 8's fix - produced six more findings, every one in prose round 8 had written to close the class. Two rules came out of it. FIRST: make the property derived rather than remembered, and put the guarantee at the boundary it is claimed about; where it cannot be derived, DELETE the claim rather than narrow it, because a narrower false sentence is still false and a pointer to the function that owns the property cannot go stale. Deletion was the fix that finally held, three separate times. SECOND: never restate a measured number in prose. Five instances here were hand-typed figures that drifted - a cap of 200 restated 250 lines from its slice(0,200), a 'low hundreds of bytes' ceiling measured at 2030, a count of 'two routes' that went stale within the same session when a third arrived, and a table-row citation of verifier.ts:972-981 that the fix's own three added comment lines pushed to 975-984. Derive the figure from the constant, or point at the assertion that measures it.
reusePrompt: About to write a comment or doc that states what nearby code guarantees, or to type a number into prose? Search this: claim wider than code, derived not remembered, delete rather than narrow.

summary: When repeated repair rounds keep finding the same defect class, the boundary is usually wrong, not the fix - declare a stopping rule in advance and honour it.
trigger: A third or later repair round in the same seam finds a defect of the same shape as the ones before it.
lesson: Before round 8 I pre-committed in writing: if the next round finds another FUNDAMENTAL defect in the bounding machinery, CHK-004 switches to outcome B - ship the ceiling, diagnostics and regression tests, downgrade the bounding to what it actually is, commit a rationale, and move the guarantee to its own story. Round 9 found five more, and two review lanes plus the cross-vendor reviewer independently recommended the same extraction. The decisive fact was structural rather than about effort: the guarantee needed a writer-owned serialize-measure-write boundary in core/store.ts, and that file was outside the story's allowedModify - so no amount of care on this side of the seam could build it. Declaring the rule in advance is what made stopping a decision rather than a retreat, and stating the reason as scope rather than as difficulty is what made the follow-up scopeable. Two mechanics that mattered: check FIRST that no immutable pinned selector binds to the claim you are about to withdraw - none of B-3434's 24 pins asserted a guarantee, which is why outcome B was compatible with every receipt - and resolve the deferred findings as partially_mitigated with the transcripts, not as fixed.
reusePrompt: Third repair round in the same seam finding the same shape of defect? Search: stopping rule, outcome B, deferral by scope not by difficulty.

summary: Cross-vendor review caught what four Claude lanes missed in four consecutive rounds, but its findings gate nothing until a lane reproduces them.
trigger: Running a real codex exec review as host-B alongside Claude reviewer lanes, or deciding whether cross-vendor review is worth its cost.
lesson: Six genuine codex exec reviews ran against B-3434. In four consecutive rounds codex found a real defect that four Claude lanes at the same revision had missed, including one inside a correction written to fix the previous one: the double-serialization divergence (reported 82 bytes, 36,000,077 on disk through the real StoryStore), the unguarded builder retry inside measureWith's catch, the false claim that the writer-owned boundary made F-036 moot when the reduction loop runs upstream of any writer, and a work-order remedy prescribing measurePersistedEvidenceBytes - the duplicated store format that F-033 identifies - in the same paragraph that declared F-033 closed. That last one was in wording I passed through verbatim without reading it back against F-033. So the cost is repaid on documentation-only rounds too, not just code rounds. The gap: isReviewerAgent requires a registered reviewerLane, and cross-host findings are filed under main, which has none - so they gate NOTHING. The working protocol is to have the owning Claude lane reproduce each claim BY EXECUTION and refile under its own lane, crediting codex explicitly as first surfacer so its work is not laundered; a lane that cannot reproduce a claim must decline to file it.
reusePrompt: Planning a cross-vendor review round, or wondering why a codex finding did not block the gate? Search: cross-host findings gate nothing, reviewerLane, refile under own lane.

summary: The validate suite sits about 2 percent under its 900s watchdog, so registering any command tips it over - and the env override that rescues it is baked into the admissibility digest.
trigger: lattice validate or story_advance aborts with 'exceeded max timeout 900000ms', or you are about to add an entry to validate.commands.
lesson: Measured on B-3434: 96 commands summed to 879,647 ms and finished at 889.7s, roughly a one percent margin. Registering one additional 3.5s RED harness took it to 97 commands and 931,983 ms, and the next run aborted with no evidence written. commandCliMaxBudget in core/done-required-timeout-budget.ts gives done_required_validate and done_prepare a config-DERIVED budget but hands validate and story_advance a flat 15*60_000 default, which silently goes stale as the suite grows; quorum-submit-smoke alone is 317s, 36 percent of the whole suite. The workaround is LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, which effectiveCommandCliMaxBudget honours as an explicit override - but it is NOT in VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST, so it is baked into effectiveEnvironmentDigest and will mismatch the next consumer's recomputation. Set it ONLY on the standalone validate, never on a gate command: assessStoredValidationPassAdmissibility checks command, JSON validity, allPass, coverage snapshot, freshness bindings and dirty tree - and NOT the environment digest - so a standalone run under a raised watchdog still produces a stored PASS that story_advance will reuse and skip the rerun.
reusePrompt: validate aborting at 900000ms, or adding an entry to validate.commands? Search: validate watchdog ceiling, LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS digest, stored PASS reuse.

summary: A regression harness that passes when a reviewer runs it by hand is not the same claim as a harness wired into the standing suite.
trigger: A story creates a new packages/main/tests/red/*.mjs harness or a new *-smoke.ts task.
lesson: B-3434's own RED harness went twelve review rounds and four reviewer lanes without anyone noticing it was never registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands. Every checklist selector bound to a DIRECT invocation of the harness by path, so 'the regression passes' and 'the regression is wired into the suite' stayed silently distinct claims, and the repository would not have run it on anyone else's change. Only the full validate run caught it, through the repository's own guard red-b49d4-harness-registration.mjs, which demands every tests/red member be either registered or listed in REGISTRATION_EXCLUSIONS with a stated reason. Two side effects worth knowing: the failure cascades, since red-b49d4-registration-derivation.mjs's DECISION_RECORD_IS_LIVE_AND_AUDITED and NEWCOMER_MIRROR_IS_FAITHFUL rows both go red downstream of the registration failure and all three clear from one line; and REAL_CONFIG_BYTE_UNMODIFIED goes red on any UNCOMMITTED lattice.config.json edit, reporting 'M lattice.config.json' from git status even when the sha is unchanged, so commit the config before running the standing suite.
reusePrompt: Created a new red harness or smoke task? Search: harness registration guard, registered or excluded with a reason, passes-by-hand is not wired-in.

summary: done_prepare --mergeMain on a hot main can pull another story's change into a file yours owns, zeroing the quorum and forcing a TEST to DEV to REVIEW re-anchor.
trigger: Running done_prepare --mergeMain while other stories are landing on main, especially when your story owns a widely-edited file.
lesson: B-3434 reached TEST with everything green - 41 findings resolved, four lane passes, a full-3x2 quorum, 97/97 validate, a signed delivery check. done_prepare --mergeMain then merged main twice in a row and the second merge brought another story's 32/31-line change into packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts, a file B-3434 owned. storyFilesHash moved, the quorum went to 0/3, every lane pass and the delivery check went stale. quorum_submit refused correctly and in the right words: 'quorum_submit will not fabricate a floor quorum without a real review.' review_run_start is not available in TEST, so the only honest route is story_advance back to DEV then REVIEW - which needs dev_memory_preflight_ack first, and needs lattice dispatch --agentType=lattice-review-<lane> per lane before review_run_start will bind. Scope the re-review to merge INTERACTION rather than a fresh audit: grep the merge diff for your own symbols, check whether the three-way merge silently lost one of your hunks, and re-check any line-number citation in your prose. Before starting, git rev-list --count HEAD..main - if main has stopped moving, the cascade will not repeat.
reusePrompt: Quorum zeroed or lane passes stale right after done_prepare --mergeMain? Search: hot main storyFilesHash cascade, TEST to DEV to REVIEW re-anchor, dispatch before review_run_start.

summary: Closeout only converges if every artifact-producing action stops before the next one starts; each write invalidates the bindings made before it.
trigger: Driving a story from DEV through REVIEW to DONE, especially one that merges main or resolves findings during closeout.
lesson: Every commit touching a story-owned file invalidates every reviewer receipt, prompt envelope and evidence binding recorded before it — and a finding-resolution commit, a waiver rewrite and a delivery reviewer writing delivery-check.json all count. B-7dff paid three extra full review rounds to that, twice after I had already written the rule down. Evidence refresh is self-invalidating and can need two passes. A validate or npm test run that overlaps any metadata commit fails with "full-suite identity drift", which reads like a test failure but is not. Working order that converges: merge main first, rebuild so dist matches merged source, re-execute stale evidence, THEN run reviewers, then quorum_submit, then advance, writing nothing in between. quorum_submit needs a current-round pass from every active lane and review_pass_set is REVIEW-only, so submit quorum before advancing to TEST or the lanes strand.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for closeout identity drift or reviewer receipt invalidation before starting any TEST to DONE sequence.

summary: Pinning a verification selector to a prose line containing a count kills the intent permanently once the tree grows past that number.
trigger: Writing checklist userSees text or a verification pin selector during PLAN.
lesson: B-7dff pinned CHK-001:happy:0 to "full-suite: 47/47 passed" and CHK-005:happy:0 to a plan-count line. main later added two suite members and three validate commands, so both selectors became unmatchable and both intents needed permanent waivers — the pins are immutable by design (checklist.ts verificationIntentProtectedPhases blocks edits outside PLAN) and no pin-repair command exists. The same mistake also put an absolute 1006s wall time into an acceptance clause, which a slower host then falsified. Pin a stable marker id emitted by the command (VI-OK STORY-CHKNNN-SOMETHING), never a count, a duration, a jobs value or any prose conclusion line. This has now cost B-49d4, B-8df9 and B-7dff a finding each.
reusePrompt: Before writing a userSees string or a verification selector, search dev-memory for pin selector count.

summary: When a gate refuses, look for the exit the repo already provides before improvising a waiver, a relabel or a new story.
trigger: Any Proof-or-Stop gate refusal during PLAN, REVIEW or closeout.
lesson: Three times in one story the first instinct was worse than what already existed. A waiver was written for a receipt that the documented commandTimeoutMs override could have minted — the override is described in CLAUDE.md, in context from turn one. A whole follow-up story was drafted asserting four miscalibrated thresholds without checking main, which had already fixed two of them; it was discarded the same day. An evidence row kind was changed from logic_test to integration_test to satisfy a milestone, with a note claiming the command spawns child processes when it does not. Reviewers caught all three. On refusal: re-read the refusal text (it usually names the field), --help the refusing command for an override, grep CLAUDE.md for the error token, and check what main already does before asserting anything about repo-level behaviour.
reusePrompt: On any gate refusal, search dev-memory for sanctioned exit before writing a waiver.

summary: TEST-to-DONE converges only if EVERY mandatory closeout write happens before the reviewers, including the two that no tool reminds you about.
trigger: Driving a story from TEST to DONE, especially after a closeout merge from main.
lesson: B-7dff needed six DONE attempts. Each failed because some gate-mandated write landed after the reviewer receipts and invalidated them. The complete order, in one uninterrupted pass: (1) summary_set, (2) the lattice-review-delivery reviewer writing delivery-check.json, (3) dev_memory_finish_decision — this one is DONE-mandatory and perturbs storyFilesHash because .lattice/dev-memory/experience.jsonl is NOT in the runtime-artifact-registry exclusion list, (4) rebind EVERY waiver by hand with verification_evidence_add, (5) verification_evidence_refresh_stale for the command-backed rows, (6) the reviewers, (7) quorum_submit, (8) story_advance TEST, (9) done_prepare, (10) story_advance DONE. Steps 3 and 4 are the ones that ambush you. Also note reviewers can only record in REVIEW and quorum_submit needs a current pass from every active lane, so a story that reaches TEST with a lane short must round-trip.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for closeout convergence order before starting any TEST to DONE sequence.

summary: verification_evidence_refresh_stale is structurally blind to waivers, so a waiver binding drifts silently until done_intent_equivalence_check refuses DONE.
trigger: Relying on verification_evidence_refresh_stale --dryRun to answer whether a story evidence is current.
lesson: evidence-refresh.ts filters waivers in refreshOnlyDrift/isWaiver BEFORE checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit runs, so --dryRun reports "No stale verification evidence" while waiver bindings are arbitrarily far out of date. On B-7dff both permanent waivers were stale, one of them 106 commits behind, and neither ever appeared in a refresh report. milestone_status DOES flag it but disclaims being a lifecycle gate, which led two reviewers to call it benign lag; done_intent_equivalence_check consumes the same coverage and blocks DONE on it. Rebind waivers by hand with verification_evidence_add, same text, before the reviewers run. To check honestly, run checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit over every row yourself rather than trusting the refresh report. Filed as story B-0f97.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for waiver blind spot when refresh reports no stale evidence but a gate says stale.

summary: The convergence breaker gates every takeover-carrying command, so --takeover cannot be used to clear a freeze; borrow the owner session id instead.
trigger: A story is FROZEN by the convergence breaker and the owner lease belongs to a different or stale session.
lesson: enforceConvergenceBreakerGate returns early only when the command is neither story_advance NOR carries --takeover/--forceTakeover. So story_resume --ack --takeover trips the breaker, while story_resume --ack without takeover trips the owner-lease gate — a deadlock. The escape is to run story_resume from a real TTY with LATTICE_SESSION_ID set to the CURRENT owner session id (session_brief prints it), so no takeover flag is needed and the lease gate passes. isInteractiveAckAllowed also requires a TTY and no CI/LATTICE_AUTOPILOT, so an agent session can never clear a freeze — this is deliberate and must be handed to the human. Watch the owner id: running session_brief with an explicit LATTICE_SESSION_ID transfers the lease to that id, so the id to borrow may have changed since the freeze.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for convergence breaker deadlock when takeover and lease block each other.

summary: DONE-required evidence binds the producing process env, so the session that runs done_required_validate must be the one that runs story_advance DONE.
trigger: Handing a closeout between an agent session and a human terminal, or setting timeout env vars for one command but not the next.
lesson: effectiveEnvironmentDigest includes PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS and PROOF_OR_STOP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS (they are not in VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST). On B-7dff the agent produced the evidence with both set; every later human invocation with a different env reported effective-environment-digest-mismatch, and a dry run without them reported a blocker that did not exist. The robust fix when closeout changes hands is to re-run done_required_validate in the FINAL session with the exact env it will use for story_advance DONE, rather than trying to reproduce the original env. Run that command exactly once: a retry at the same TEST anchor pollutes unchangedSuiteExecutions.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for effective-environment-digest-mismatch before rerunning done_required_validate.

summary: A guard that has never been observed failing is not evidence, and three guards in one story passed on exactly the defect they were written to catch.
trigger: Writing or reviewing a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check that is meant to prove a property.
lesson: Every guard needs a negative control BEFORE it is trusted: inject the exact defect it targets and confirm it fails. In B-3e16 three separate guards passed on their own target defect. verify-docs searched a whole 1400-line file so a deleted flag still matched elsewhere. verify-no-project-writes allowlisted by FILE, so a project-root write in an allowed file passed while printing a reassuring cache-derived reason. verify-clean-tree used the default warm cache, so no index rebuild fired and it measured nothing at all. Each produced specific, confident output. Also beware the control being broken rather than the guard: an `if (false && ...)` neuter can fail to compile and leave a STALE dist that reports PASS, and prefixing a condition into a compound `A || B` disables only A. A neuter must DELETE the check, and you must confirm the build succeeded and the dist actually changed.
reusePrompt: About to trust a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check? Search this before relying on it: negative control, guard passes on its own target defect, stale dist, vacuous guard.

summary: Fixing the demonstrated instance instead of the class produces a guard that is defeated again by the next spelling of the same attack.
trigger: Responding to a reviewer finding about a bypass, especially in a security or provenance check.
lesson: B-3e16 needed five versions of one write guard because each fix closed the instance shown rather than the class. The reviewer named it exactly: the class was never "single-letter alias", it was "the guard trusts the identifier name". Renaming the variable moved the instance and left the trust intact. A lexical rule cannot decide provenance, and worse, it inverted the incentive: it rejected an honestly named cache write while rewarding the rename that defeats it. The fix that held was measuring the EFFECT (run a real scan in a subprocess, hash every path, assert the repository is byte-identical), because that is primitive-agnostic and catches worker threads, child processes and sqlite alike. When a reviewer says a fix is instance-shaped, stop patching and ask what property is actually being asserted.
reusePrompt: Reviewer says a bypass is fixed but the same attack works through a different spelling? Search: instance versus class, lexical rule cannot decide provenance, measure the effect not the call.

summary: The cannotAutoSign rule is load-bearing: an independent host found twelve real defects that eleven in-session reviewer passes had approved.
trigger: Hitting review_assurance_floor, cannotAutoSign, or a host-verdict requirement and being tempted to treat it as bureaucratic friction.
lesson: In B-3e16 four reviewer lanes and a topology critic passed the story across three inventory waves. An independent host (codex, then claude via CLI) then found twelve real defects across twelve rounds, including live arbitrary code execution via an unvalidated --root, a security guard that could be defeated by a nested same-name producer, and a guard PRINTING coverage it did not have. Six of those defects were in guards written to close the previous finding. Note also that review_host_availability_probe reported all three hosts as execution_failure:timeout when codex actually worked fine when invoked directly - do not conclude no host is available from a probe timeout alone. Verdicts bind to materialHash, so a fix invalidates the pass that preceded it; re-earn it rather than submitting a verdict bound to code the host never saw.
reusePrompt: Blocked by cannotAutoSign, review escalation quorum, or a host verdict requirement? Search: independent host found what in-session lanes missed, probe timeout is not host unavailability, verdicts bind to materialHash.

summary: CLI next-step hints still print the retired "lattice dispatch" bin name, and a stale global lattice binary makes it fail plausibly instead of loudly.
trigger: Running reviewer_list, review_inventory or a REVIEW transition and reading the "Next:" line it prints.
lesson: B-a4e3 removed the dispatch aliases and CLAUDE.md mandates "proof-or-stop dispatch", but reviewer-list.ts:241, review-inventory.ts:239/251 and transition-effects.ts:254 still emit "Next: lattice dispatch ...". There is no bin/lattice in this repo, yet /opt/homebrew/bin/lattice resolves to a separate @lattice/core install reporting 0.3.257 while the repo builds 0.3.269. So copy-pasting the hint does not give command-not-found: it silently drives a twelve-version-stale binary against a different install, the same version-skew class .githooks/pre-push exists to prevent. The lattice-residue brand-prose gate misses it because its scan roots cover docs and markdown, not emitted runtime strings under packages/main/src. Any fix must also update the assert.match pins in review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:218/385 and lattice-parallel-wave-smoke.ts:338, which pin the old spelling. Note gap_log could not record this: it fails with invalid_binding_shape because B-META findings.json is a flat array with no provenance chain.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for "lattice dispatch" or "brand-prose runtime strings" before touching reviewer_list / review-inventory / transition-effects next-step output, or when extending verify-lattice-residue scan roots.

summary: A reviewer "cannot find the cited artifact" claim is often a search-scope error, not missing evidence -- verify before acting on it.
trigger: A REVIEW lane reports that evidence cited in a signed record does not correspond to any real artifact.
lesson: In B-3e16 the quality lane passed but flagged that assertLoaderArgumentProvenance and its "14 permanent mutants", cited in a signed review_escalation_fallback record, could not be found. It searched packages/graph and packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts. The guard actually lives in packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts:5162, is invoked at :5653, and its mutant array holds exactly 14 tuple-form entries, each asserted to (a) really differ from the original, (b) keep the pinned argument byte-identical, (c) change the AST fingerprint, and (d) still trip the provenance pin when scanned with the MUTANT OWN fingerprint -- so re-pinning cannot launder a mutant. The evidence was accurate; only the search scope was wrong. Note the mutants use tuple form ["label", code], so a regex for /label:/ finds zero and looks like confirmation of the reviewer claim. Confirm with grep -rln across the whole package before filing a finding against signed evidence.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for "search-scope error" or "cited artifact not found" before filing a finding that signed evidence references a nonexistent artifact.

summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest hashes the whole ambient environment minus a deny-list, so per-invocation host/terminal/OTEL variables make a DONE-required receipt unverifiable from any other shell.
trigger: done_prepare or lifecycle_check reports effective-environment-digest-mismatch[N] even though done_required_validate just returned PASS
lesson: The digest is recomputed at read time from the reader's own environment and compared to the value stored in done-required-evidence.json, so ANY ambient value that differs between the writing process and the verifying process breaks it. VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST is digest-pinned by VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEYS_DIGEST and must stay byte-stable, so new keys are stripped at the filter seam in effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment (see HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS) rather than appended to the pinned list. But the leak has a long tail from independent sources: Claude Code (CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN), cmux (CMUX_TERMINAL_LIFECYCLE_ID, CMUX_TAB_ID, CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID, CMUX_PORT*), Alacritty (ALACRITTY_LOG/SOCKET, PID-embedded), tmux (TMUX, PID-embedded), macOS (LaunchInstanceID), and OTEL (TRACEPARENT, whose span-id regenerates per invocation and therefore defeats any deny-list). Do not chase these one at a time: each fix costs a full lane re-earn plus a ~5 minute DONE-required suite. Instead launch BOTH the receipt writer and every later verifier from one identically-stripped environment via an env -u wrapper script; the digest then matches because both sides see the same environment. Verify stability first by running buildDoneRequiredExecutionIdentity twice through the wrapper and comparing effectiveEnvironmentDigest. The architectural fix (allow-list of semantically relevant vars such as PATH/NODE_OPTIONS/CI/locale instead of a deny-list) belongs in its own story.
reusePrompt: Search for effective-environment-digest-mismatch, TRACEPARENT, or done-required receipt unverifiable across shells before adding another key to HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS.
